parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A capacitor of capacitance *C₁* is connected in series with a second capacitor of capacitance *C₂*.

Show that the combined capacitance *C* of the two capacitors is given by

$\frac{1}{C}=\frac{1}{C_1}+\frac{1}{C_2}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Three identical capacitors, each of capacitance *C*, are connected in a network as shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The variation of the charge *Q* with the potential difference (p.d.) *V* between the terminals X and Y is shown in Fig. 5.2.

[[fig:f2]]

Show that *C* is equal to 44 μF.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: The capacitor network in Fig. 5.1 is charged and then connected to a resistor of resistance 54 kΩ. The capacitor network discharges through the resistor.
parts.text: Determine the time constant *τ* of the circuit. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the time taken for the discharge current to reduce to 15% of the initial discharge current.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A capacitor is connected across the top branch of a rectangular network, with two capacitors in series along the bottom branch between terminals X and Y.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A straight line on a graph of charge Q in μC against potential difference V in V rises from 0 to 400 μC at 6 V.
